This summer I went to a Dead and Company concert at the Klipsch music center in Indiana. Me and a friend had lawn seats. During intermission a stranger came up to us and gave us two tickets for closer seats to use for the second set, some very good seats I might add. Almost dead center, about five rows back from the pit.

The very next night I went to the same venue to see a Florida Georgia Line / Cole Swindell concert with my sister and parents. We got into the venue and my Dad distributed the tickets to the family. Our four seats included the two seats my friend and I had randomly received the night before. I was freaking out, definitely the weirdest coincidence I have ever personally experienced.

I went to my first real concert when I was 14 with two of my friends. We had balcony seats. One of my friends wanted to find someone to get us on the floor. So the three of us are just standing in the lobby looking around. One of my friends says fuck it and goes back to sit. I went with him. 5 minutes later my other friend comes back and says to follow him because he found some girl to get us and the floor and he already paid her $20. We're like "she probably took off", but I followed him while the other guy stayed behind. The girl was waiting for us. So we followed her and we came to the door going to the floor and my friend and I stopped while the girl keeps walking and hands the guy checking tickets the $20. The girl said "come on". So we just walked onto the floor and straight to the stage. At one point during the concert I looked around and saw everyone having fun. Then I looked at the balcony. Everybody was just sitting and staring.

Here are some from my childhood.

 

I was riding a small tricycle big-wheel. I see this probably 3" tall bit of concrete jutting out of the grass in my neighbors yard. I'm like 5-6.

I think "aw yeah that'd be cool to jump", so I do my best to jump it. Of course, being in grass, I didn't gain any speed and just stopped when I hit it. I got mad and thought "fine, but I'll go over it no matter what." I kick the pedals as hard as I can.

One of the spokes hits my achilles tendon and carves off a nice bit of skin. Like 2" long. 40% is number from the pain and the other 60% is still alive. It hurts quite a lot.

I sit there, and in my childhood wisdom, grab the skin and just yank as hard as I can.

The whole thing comes off and starts bleeding quite a bit so I run to the house and I forget what happens after that.

I have a nice big scar on my tendon due to this.

 

When I was 4, my brother was tossing me on our parents bed. He was 16. I was a late child.

He keeps throwing me to make me bounce high and I keep telling him to do it higher.

Eventually, I am 1 foot from the ceiling. This time though, I veer off the bed and hit my forehead headfirst onto the corner of the side table.

I just close my eyes as hard as I can. I can feel the warm blood running on my face, but no pain. My brother picks me up and takes me into the kitchen where our family was. He hands me to my mom and immediately passes out (my mom told me this later) from seeing the blood.

The next thing I know, it's 3 days later and my mom is taking a butterfly bandage off my forehead.

The thing is, I don't feel like I'm missing any memories. It's like when you are put under general anasthesia. You're out one moment and awake the next. Very weird. I also have a scar for that.

 

When I was 8 or so, my family went camping. My cousin and I are playing while our parents are just sitting and talking around the fire. She has her bike and I'm just chasing her around as she rides it.

There's this very steep hill up to a road beside our camp grounds. You can see where this is going.

I get my cousin to go to the top of the hill with me and we both get on her small bike, me in front. We try to ride it down together. It doesn't go well. We lose control quickly and tumble down.

At the bottom, somehow, a chunk (not just the surface) of skin is missing on my calf on one side. I assume spokes since I was on the front with my leg near the tire when it happened. I had to sleep in pain that night as we didn't have anything to wrap the wound in and it was otherwise fine.

I also have a large scar from that.

 

When I was 10 or so, I was riding bikes with my step-brother behind a local grocery store. There was a broken shopping cart nearby and we got "smart" again. We took one of the sides of the shopping cart and laid it up against a large brick to make a ramp. These were nice bikes so I could've gotten air on this, I'm sure even now.

Now, the side of the shopping cart wasn't laying against the brick entirely so my step-brother held it in place while I sped up to jump it.

Next thing I know, I'm at home with my face hurting. The a-hole had laid the cart down at the last second to mess with me. I hit the brick and did a front flip hitting face first into concrete. We were about a 5 minute walk from my house so my step-brother left me there while he ran to get my mom.

I think I chipped a tooth due to that.

 

Once when I was at home somewhere around the age of 7, I was walking around just kinda bored. I stepped on a splinter in a part of the house that was under construction at the time. This splinter stuck out of my foot by about 0.5". It felt bad though.

I went into my parent's bathroom and sat and looked at it for a minute thinking on what to do. Then I decided to just take it out. I ripped it out in one pull.

The splinter had went into my foot at a 90 degree angle. Meaning, it went directly in and penetrated it deeply because of that. It was over an inch long. My foot bled a lot.

 

My mom had told me not to go to bed with bubble gum in my mouth. I didn't listen. It ended up in my hair. When I realized this, I got scared she would get mad at me. She was not abusive, but I didn't like getting in trouble.

I proceeded to pull on the gum until it was all out of my hair. Unfortunately, the hair came with it.

I had a bald spot at the age of 8 in the dead center of my head for about 9 months the size of a quarter. When the hair eventually grew back, it was auburn red. My natural hair-color was black/dark-brown. My mom's hair color was auburn red. I liked that tbh. I wish my hair was her hair color.

 

We used to go to a water filled quarry for the summer. My uncle built a large diving platform there out of scrap metal. He hung a long rope with a triangle handle on it to swing off of.

When I was 5 or so, I decided I wanted to try it. They eventually let me. I didn't let go though. On the way back, because the rope was longer than needed to be easy to grab again, I hit my side on the rocks. Fortunately, I had a life vest on so it took some of the impact, but part of my side looks deformed to me and I wonder if that's why.

It probably isn't. It wasn't that bad and I didn't have a broken anything, but I don't know.

 

When I was 16, I had a Red 1987 Chevrolet Silverado as my first vehicle. My mother had spent the good part of 2 years looking for one identical to my dads that wasn't excessively expensive. My dad had died in a vehicle accident when I was 12 and I looked a lot like him, and she wanted that as my first vehicle.

Well, my mother passed away when I was 16. A few months later, I was driving my step-brother (the same one who put down the side of the shopping cart) to our shared orthodontist appointment 30 minutes away. Now, I didn't know anything about vehicles. I'm in IT now and I do computers.

Literally 4 miles from home, the engine block catches on fire. It had started smoking so we had stopped to look at it on the side of the road before and it wasn't on fire then, but I do remember seeing a wire melted to the engine block.

What I imagine happened was that the wire had sparked a fire on the insulation under the hood. This quickly consumed the vehicle.

In our teenage brilliance, we had parked the truck (now on fire) not 50 feet away from a large propane canister. Large, as in, 18-wheeler size.
